text:
Jordan: handing off night shift. I'm primary until 02:00 UTC, Priya is secondary. Quick summary: started seeing elevated 429s from embedding-service (~18:10 UTC), incident-bot opened INC-3890. Root cause looks like a KV-cache eviction storm on a subset of nodes in eu-west-1.

incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-3890 created at 18:17 UTC — embedding-kv-cache-throttle. Severity: P2. Pages: Jordan, Priya. Affected: Hosted API region eu-west-1 (select customers experiencing intermittent 429/timeout). Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/embedding-kv-eviction

Samir: short log dump — observed repeated cache miss storms after a pod restart chain. Machines with older kernel patches hit higher eviction rates. I bumped the replica count and disabled aggressive eviction on the problem pool.

Samir: actions taken so far:
```
# scale embed workers
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/embed-workers --replicas=8
# disable eviction flag on node pool
gcloud compute instances update-group embed-pool --update-additional-metadata eviction=disabled
```

Maya: monitoring: error rate peaked ~17% at 18:12, now down to ~2% as of 19:08. p95 token latency went from 640ms -> 180ms. No new customer Slack/SRE alerts after 18:45.

Jordan: current status — degraded -> stabilizing. There is still elevated retry traffic and a handful of tail 429s (~0.2% requests). We put a temporary low-priority throttle rule to protect SLO-critical routes.

Priya: note — I removed the canary config that was causing uneven cache warming; also opened a ticket with infra to backport kernel patch to the older worker image. infra ticket ID: INF-7721.

Jordan: coverage notes for the handoff: Priya will be offline 23:45–00:15 UTC for a personal appointment; Maya will cover immediate paging during that window (Maya confirmed). After that, Priya will be reachable for escalation.

Maya: suggested next steps (short):
- keep embed-workers at +2 replicas for 4h, then evaluate
- watch eviction rate metric: infra.eviction.rate (alert threshold 0.5%)
- run the canonical cache warmup for suspect models: `/scripts/warmup_embeddings.sh --region eu-west-1`
- schedule kernel patch rollout to the problematic node pool (INF-7721)

Jordan: open action items (owner):
- Samir: follow up on INF-7721 and link patch PR (ETA 24h)
- Priya: confirm rollback window for the canary config (ETA before 22:00 UTC)
- Maya: keep a watch on customer-facing error rate for next 6 hours and escalate if >1%

Jordan: mitigation playbook excerpt for whoever inherits (short):
1) Check incident dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/incidents/INC-3890
2) If eviction.rate > 0.5% -> scale embed-workers to 10 replicas and enable temporary route-throttling for non-SLO routes
3) If error rate stays >3% for 15m -> open bridge and call infra on-call, escalate to engineering lead

Priya: FYI — I left a pinned message in the runbook with the exact kubectl commands and the warmup script output. Also added a short note for support: "Customers experiencing intermittent 429s in eu-west-1 were mitigated by scaling and cache warmup; ongoing watch."

Jordan: end-state before handoff: incident still open, impact reduced to negligible (few retries only), actions scheduled and owners assigned. Primary handoff: Jordan -> Priya (primary), Maya covers while Priya briefly offline.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-11-04T18:05Z: hotfix/kv-eviction-tune applied to embed-workers (canary 2/6). No errors from canary.

Jordan: last note — be ready to flip the canary off if we see churn after 21:30 UTC. Otherwise, check back-in at 00:00 UTC for status update from Priya. Thanks — :thumbsup:
